skill.name: generating-sorbet-inline
skill.description: Adds Sorbet inline sig blocks to Ruby source files and helps validate method-level type signatures.
skill.summary: Generate Sorbet inline signatures for Ruby methods using sig blocks.
skill.author: DmitryPogrebnoy

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, Sorbet sig syntax, documentation URLs, Ruby Hash#fetch, and bundled reference examples. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found. The main residual risk is the instruction to run Sorbet validation commands in the user project.

remediation.issue: Validation commands are written as a required step.
remediation.suggestion: Make srb tc and bundle exec srb tc opt-in, and instruct the agent to ask before running project commands.

remediation.issue: Bundled Packwerk reference code triggers many static analyzer alerts.
remediation.suggestion: Label reference/sorbet_examples as non-executable examples or reduce it to minimal signature snippets.

Generate Sorbet type signatures using `sig {}` blocks directly in Ruby source files. Sorbet signatur
- You MUST NOT use `T.untyped`. Infer the proper type instead.
- You MUST NOT use `T.unsafe` - it bypasses type checking entirely.
- You MUST NOT use `T.cast` - it forces types without verification.
- You MUST prepend any command with `bundle exec` if the project has Gemfile.
- You MUST use `sig { }` block syntax for method signatures.
- You MUST add `extend T::Sig` to classes/modules before using `sig`.
- You MUST NOT use or generate `.rbi` files. This skill is for inline signatures only.
- You MUST preserve the existing `# typed:` sigil level if one exists. Do not upgrade or change stri
- Note existing `# typed:` sigil level at the top of the file.
1. First, check if the file already has a `# typed:` sigil at the top:
- **If no sigil exists**: Add `# typed: true` as a sensible default (allows gradual typing).
3. Then add type signatures using `sig {}` blocks:
- Review all signatures and replace `T.untyped` with proper types.
- Use `T.untyped` only as a last resort when type cannot be determined.

semantic_findings.title: Validation Command Execution Requires Trust
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run srb tc or bundle exec srb tc to validate signatures. These commands execute tooling from the user Ruby environment and should require explicit approval in untrusted projects.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The validation section clearly names shell commands. The intent is legitimate type checking, but it still asks the agent to execute project-local tooling.

content.value_statement: Ruby teams often need typed method contracts without moving logic into RBI files. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through adding Sorbet sig blocks directly in source files.
actual_capabilities: Adds # typed: true when a Ruby file has no Sorbet sigil.
Preserves an existing # typed: sigil unless the user requests a change.
Adds extend T::Sig before generating method signatures.
Generates sig blocks for methods, constructors, and attribute readers.
Uses nearby code context to avoid T.untyped where possible.
Suggests Sorbet validation with srb tc or bundle exec srb tc.
limitations: It focuses on inline method signatures and does not create RBI files.
It may need user input when Ruby metaprogramming hides parameter or return types.
Validation commands should be reviewed before running in untrusted repositories.
It does not guarantee every inferred type matches runtime behavior.

use_cases.title: Type a Small Ruby Class
use_cases.description: Add Sorbet sig blocks to a class with constructors, readers, and simple instance methods.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Gradual Typing Pull Request
use_cases.description: Convert selected files to inline Sorbet signatures while keeping the existing typed sigil policy.

use_cases.title: Review Existing Sorbet Signatures
use_cases.description: Check generated signatures for T.untyped use, missing extend T::Sig declarations, and mismatched return types.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Signatures
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Sorbet inline signatures to this Ruby file. Preserve the current typed sigil and explain any uncertain type choices.

prompt_templates.title: Avoid Untyped Parameters
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with stronger type quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate inline sig blocks for these methods. Use the implementation and tests to avoid T.untyped unless no reliable type can be inferred.

prompt_templates.title: Annotate Attributes and Constructors
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for model-style Ruby classes
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Sorbet signatures for the constructor, attr_reader methods, attr_writer methods, and public instance methods in this class.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Refine Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a full typing pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Sorbet inline signatures, identify likely type errors, and suggest safe refinements before running any validation command.

output_examples.input: A Ruby class with an initializer, two attribute readers, and a greeting method.
output_examples.output: The file receives a typed sigil if missing, extend T::Sig, and method-level signatures for each public API.

output_examples.input: A service object with keyword arguments and an optional value.
output_examples.output: The generated signatures describe required keywords, nullable values, and the method return type in Sorbet syntax.

output_examples.input: A file that already uses # typed: strict and some existing sig blocks.
output_examples.output: The skill preserves the strict sigil, fills missing signatures, and flags any remaining uncertain types for review.

best_practices: Provide the full Ruby file and related tests when asking for inferred types.
Review every generated type before committing changes.
Run Sorbet validation only after approving the command and repository context.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to generate RBI files for this workflow.
Do not accept T.untyped for unclear methods without a follow-up review.
Do not run validation commands automatically in untrusted repositories.

faq.question: Does this skill create RBI files?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for inline sig blocks inside Ruby source files.

faq.question: Will it change my typed sigil?
faq.answer: It preserves existing sigils unless you explicitly ask for a different strictness level.

faq.question: Can it handle attr_reader and attr_writer methods?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for signatures on common attribute declarations.

faq.question: Does it use T.untyped?
faq.answer: The skill tries to avoid T.untyped and asks for more context when types are unclear.

faq.question: Should I run the suggested validation command?
faq.answer: Review the repository first. Run srb tc or bundle exec srb tc only when you trust the project context.

faq.question: Is this useful for new Sorbet projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It can add a starting # typed: true sigil and basic inline signatures for gradual typing.
